title: Container Bookings: Completeness of a Booking's Change Account for Goodwill
content:
Goodwill on a Container Bookings customer roll fee is weighed only against a booking whose change account is complete. This page defines what a complete change account is.

## Principle

A goodwill decision on a roll fee presupposes a full and settled picture of what the booking's changes have cost. The change account is complete when every discharge-port change that owes a fee under its own rules has its change-of-destination fee entry on the charge history, and every customer roll in excess of the product's free customer rolls has its customer roll fee entry there too.

## How completeness is measured

- **Destination changes without their fee:** the count of discharge-port amendment log entries reduced by the count of change-of-destination fee entries.
- **Customer rolls without their fee:** where the roll notices naming the customer as cause are more numerous than the product's free customer rolls, their number less the free customer rolls, and otherwise none; from that, the customer roll fee entries are deducted.
- The account is complete when neither measure is above zero.

## Changes that owe nothing

A change that owes no fee under its own rules cannot leave the account incomplete. That is so where the product does not accept a change of port of discharge (for destination changes), where the product charges no customer roll fee (for customer rolls), and where the booking has no chargeable container left once the containers of a rejected dangerous-goods acceptance are set aside (for both).

## Hypothetical cases

| Destination change log entries / fee entries | Customer roll notices / free rolls / roll fee entries | Complete? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 / 1 | 2 / 1 / 1 | yes |
| 1 / 0 | 2 / 1 / 1 | no |
| 0 / 0 | 3 / 1 / 1 | no |
| 1 / 0, on a product that accepts no destination change | 1 / 1 / 0 | yes |

The counts and allowances are invented.
